args: Native mobile interface design conventions that a DESIGNER must decide, for iOS and Android, current as of 2026. Narrow scope — platform design law only, not implementation code. Cover exactly these: (1) Apple's current design language and Human Interface Guidelines direction as of 2025-2026, including the Liquid Glass material introduced at WWDC 2025 for iOS 26 — what it actually is, where it applies, what it demands of a designer, and what Apple says NOT to do with it; (2) Google's Material 3 and Material 3 Expressive — current status, what Expressive changed, and its stated research basis; (3) navigation models and when each is correct: iOS tab bar vs Android bottom navigation bar, navigation stack and back behavior including Android's system back and predictive back, sheets and modals, iOS NavigationSplitView vs Android navigation rail; (4) the numeric specifications a designer must hit: minimum touch target sizes (Apple 44pt vs Material 48dp — verify both from primary sources), default type scales and body text sizes, spacing and margin baselines, and corner radius conventions; (5) safe areas and system regions — status bar, home indicator, Dynamic Island, display cutouts, edge-to-edge and the Android 15+ mandatory edge-to-edge change; (6) gesture systems and their conflicts — iOS interactive pop gesture and Android back-swipe versus author-built horizontal swipe affordances such as carousels and swipe-to-delete; (7) what genuinely differs between the two platforms such that a single design cannot serve both, and where a cross-platform neutral design is legitimate. Prioritize primary sources only: developer.apple.com Human Interface Guidelines, m3.material.io, developer.android.com. Reject blog restatements where a primary source exists.
